questions.question: Developmental biology is the study of a process whereby a single cell divides and selectively activates expression of what?
questions.explanation: Developmental biology studies how a single cell selectively activates gene expression.

questions.question: The process by which a single cell divides to produce a complex organism involves selective activation of what?
questions.explanation: Selective activation of gene expression is key to forming a complex organism from a single cell.

questions.question: Which of the following is a required process to form an embryo?
questions.explanation: Gametes forming and fusing is a fundamental process required to form an embryo.

questions.question: The process of cells multiplying during embryo formation is known as what?
questions.explanation: Growth refers to the multiplication of cells during embryonic development.

questions.question: Anterior/Posterior, Dorsal/Ventral, and Left/Right are examples of what type of determination?
questions.explanation: These are the axes determined during embryo formation.

questions.question: The process where cells become specialized in structure and function is called what?
questions.explanation: Differentiation is the process by which cells become specialized.

questions.question: Structures are built from cells during a process known as what?
questions.explanation: Morphogenesis is the process of building structures from cells.

questions.question: Animal cells organize into sheets and move, while plant cells form structures without doing what?
questions.explanation: Plant cells form structures without moving, unlike animal cells.

questions.question: The study of a process whereby a single cell divides and selectively activates gene expression is called what?
questions.explanation: Developmental biology studies this process.

questions.question: Differentiation is a central idea of development where all cells have the same DNA but express different what?
questions.explanation: All cells have the same DNA but express different genes.

questions.question: Although all cells in a body have the same DNA, they express different genes due to their different what?
questions.explanation: Different cells express different genes because they have different tasks.

questions.question: The cellular machinery is largely made up of which type of molecules?
questions.explanation: The cellular machinery is largely made up of proteins.

questions.question: Different cells contain different proteins because they have different what?
questions.explanation: Different cells contain different proteins due to their different tasks.

questions.question: Proteins are made up of chains of amino acids encoded in the cell's what?
questions.explanation: The amino acid sequence of proteins is encoded in the cell's DNA.

questions.question: Information flows from DNA to RNA to what molecule?
questions.explanation: The central dogma states information flows from DNA to RNA to protein.

questions.question: When one gene is mutated, what is the direct consequence?
questions.explanation: A mutation in one gene typically affects one protein.

questions.question: Most organisms use information from parents and what other source to know which genes to activate?
questions.explanation: Cells use information from parents and neighbors.

questions.question: Information from parents during development is known as the cell what?
questions.explanation: Information from parents is referred to as the cell lineage.

questions.question: The unequal localization of determinants during cell division is a mechanism to generate what?
questions.explanation: Unequal localization of determinants generates asymmetry.

questions.question: What type of molecules are typically the "determinants" that are segregated during cell division?
questions.explanation: Determinants are usually proteins or mRNA.

questions.question: Cell division transfers determinants to a single daughter cell, causing the cells to become what?
questions.explanation: Transferring determinants to one daughter cell makes the cells different.

questions.question: An alternative mechanism to generate asymmetry is cell division placing daughter cells in different what?
questions.explanation: Cell division can place daughter cells in different environments, generating asymmetry.

questions.question: Different environments lead daughter cells to have different what?
questions.explanation: Different environments lead to different cell fates.

questions.question: Single yeast cells "talk" to each other when they want to do what?
questions.explanation: Yeast cells communicate when they want to mate.

questions.question: In yeast, what are the names of the two cell types?
questions.explanation: The two yeast cell types are "A" and "alpha".

questions.question: In yeast, each cell type makes a specific signal and has receptors only for the opposite what?
questions.explanation: Each cell type has receptors only for the opposite signal.

questions.question: The cell-cell signals in yeast lead the cells to move together, change shape, and ultimately do what?
questions.explanation: The signals lead the yeast cells to fuse.

questions.question: The fusion of yeast cells produces what type of cell?
questions.explanation: The fusion of two yeast cells produces a diploid cell.

questions.question: Even the most simple eukaryotic organisms sense their environment, migrate, adhere, differentiate and do what?
questions.explanation: Even simple organisms sense, migrate, adhere, differentiate and interact.

questions.question: All organisms share similar cellular machinery, and all animals use this machinery in similar ways to direct what?
questions.explanation: Animals use similar cellular machinery to direct embryonic development.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction requires only how many parents?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction requires only one parent.

questions.question: Offspring produced by asexual reproduction are an exact copy of the parent, known as a what?
questions.explanation: Offspring that are exact copies are called clones.

questions.question: Organisms that reproduce asexually cannot develop much variety because they are doing what to the original organism?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction copies the original organism exactly, limiting variety.

questions.question: The lack of variety in asexual reproduction does not allow for what process?
questions.explanation: Without variety, evolution of the species cannot occur.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction takes a relatively short period of time and can produce how many offspring?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction can produce 1 to 100s of offspring.

questions.question: Which of the following is a method of asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Binary fission is a method of asexual reproduction.

questions.question: Single-celled organisms like Amoeba and Paramecium reproduce asexually by dividing into two equal halves, a process called what?
questions.explanation: Dividing into two equal halves is called binary fission.

questions.question: Binary fission is a very effective way of producing many offspring when conditions are what?
questions.explanation: Binary fission is effective when conditions are good, like plenty of food and water.

questions.question: In the space of 8 hours, a Paramecium can divide, grow, and divide again, representing what type of reproduction?
questions.explanation: This rapid division is characteristic of binary fission.

questions.question: In which method of asexual reproduction does an offspring grow out of the body of the parent?
questions.explanation: Budding involves an offspring growing out of the parent's body.

questions.question: Hydra and Cactus are examples of organisms that use which method of asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Hydra and Cactus reproduce by budding.

questions.question: Which method of asexual reproduction involves an organism breaking into fragments that grow into new individuals?
questions.explanation: Fragmentation involves breaking into pieces that grow into new individuals.

questions.question: Which method of asexual reproduction involves an egg developing without fertilization?
questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis is the development of an egg without fertilization.

questions.question: The generation of asymmetry is a required process to form what?
questions.explanation: Generating asymmetry is required for embryo formation.

questions.question: What is the central idea of development?
questions.explanation: Differentiation is a central idea of development.

questions.question: The information flow from DNA to RNA to Protein is a fundamental concept in what?
questions.explanation: This is a fundamental concept in biology.

questions.question: Cell lineage provides information from which source?
questions.explanation: Cell lineage is information from parents.

questions.question: The "determinants" passed from parent to offspring are usually what type of molecules?
questions.explanation: Determinants are usually proteins or mRNA.

questions.question: Yeast cells "talk" to each other using specific signals to initiate what process?
questions.explanation: Yeast cells communicate to initiate mating.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction produces offspring that are an exact copy of the parent, meaning they are what?
questions.explanation: Asexual offspring are clones.
